title: Rollout controller: add SLO evaluator hook (flagged) + pause-only action
author: Jada Williams
description:
Summary
This PR introduces an SLO evaluation hook into the rollout controller state machine. The controller can now consult an external SLO evaluator for the exact rollout scope (service/route + model version + region + customer tier) and take a conservative automatic action.

MVP behavior in this PR is pause-only (no rollback execution). If an SLO breach is confirmed, the rollout is paused at the current step and an audit event is emitted. When SLO data is missing/stale/insufficient, we do not pause (fail-open) but we record a structured reason for visibility.

Motivation
We’ve had multiple latency/error regressions during canary/A-B rollouts where the window between detection and manual intervention is too large. This adds the wiring point so follow-on PRs can plug in:
- policy/config evaluation (thresholds, windows, debounce)
- the monitor provider adapter (burn rate + sample size)
- rollback executor (traffic shift back to baseline)

Key changes
- Adds a RolloutSloEvaluator interface and wires it into the controller loop.
- Adds a feature flag gate: rollouts.auto_slo_eval.enabled (default: false).
- Adds pause-only action outcome:
  - If evaluator returns BREACH_CONFIRMED => controller transitions to PAUSED with reason AUTO_PAUSE_SLO_BREACH.
  - If evaluator returns OK => no change.
  - If evaluator returns INSUFFICIENT_DATA / MONITOR_MISSING / MONITOR_STALE / EVAL_ERROR => no change, emit structured log + audit event w/ suppression_reason.
- Adds unit tests covering state transitions and idempotency.

Notes / non-goals
- No rollback action is executed in this PR (follow-up: rollback executor + safe traffic shift).
- No burn-rate window/debounce logic lives here; this PR only introduces the hook and the contract.
- No Console API changes here; audit event is emitted but not yet surfaced.

Implementation details
- The hook is invoked after a step has been applied (i.e., traffic split update committed) and before advancing to the next step.
- Evaluator input is a RolloutScope derived from rollout metadata:
  - service_id, route_id
  - model_id + candidate_version_id
  - region
  - customer_tier
- Controller behavior is explicitly idempotent:
  - If already PAUSED, repeated BREACH_CONFIRMED responses do not re-emit the pause action.

Testing
- Added controller unit tests:
  - pauses rollout when evaluator reports breach
  - does not pause on missing/stale/insufficient data
  - does not pause when flag disabled
  - evaluator error is treated as fail-open (no pause)
  - idempotent pause (no duplicate events)

Rollout plan
- Land behind flag (off by default).
- Enable in dev/staging for internal canaries after monitor adapter PR is ready.

Related
- Linear: ENG-4821
- Design/PRD: Auto-rollback on SLO breach integration (see Confluence)

Checklist
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Flag default is disabled
- [x] Logging does not include customer prompt content
- [x] Controller remains functional when evaluator is unset (no-op evaluator)
commits: rollouts/controller: introduce RolloutSloEvaluator interface + no-op implementation
rollouts/controller: wire evaluator into step advancement with feature flag gate
rollouts/controller: add pause outcome + reason codes for audit/logging
tests: controller state machine coverage for pause-only SLO outcome
cleanup: naming + docs/comments for evaluator contract
review_conversation:
Ethan Park (review): Can we confirm the hook is invoked after the traffic split change is persisted? If called before, we might pause based on SLOs that reflect the *previous* step.
Jada Williams (author): Good catch. Updated to invoke after ApplyStep() returns success and we have the new step_index committed. Added a unit test that asserts ordering around ApplyStep vs Evaluate().

Jordan Lee (review): The feature flag key name should match the convention used by policy engine flags (dot-separated). Also please ensure the evaluator contract makes it explicit that debounce/windows are not implemented here.
Jada Williams (author): Renamed flag to rollouts.auto_slo_eval.enabled and added docstrings in the interface clarifying controller only consumes a pre-evaluated decision.

Sean Gallagher (review): For MVP, I agree with pause-only, but I strongly prefer fail-open on monitor missing/stale to avoid accidental pauses during telemetry outages. Please add a structured audit/log reason so we can see when we’re blind.
Jada Williams (author): Implemented fail-open for MONITOR_MISSING / MONITOR_STALE / INSUFFICIENT_DATA / EVAL_ERROR and emit an audit event with suppression_reason=<reason>. No paging yet; that will come with dashboards.

Chloe Martin (review): Minor: the pause reason enum should be stable for Console. Also avoid putting rollout name strings in logs; use rollout_id.
Jada Williams (author): Updated to log rollout_id + scope fields only, and made AUTO_PAUSE_SLO_BREACH a stable string constant in audit schema.

Approvals
- Ethan Park: Approved
- Jordan Lee: Approved
- Sean Gallagher: Approved
- Chloe Martin: Approved
release_notes: Internal: Rollout controller now supports a flagged SLO evaluation hook and can auto-pause a rollout on confirmed SLO breach (pause-only; no rollback).
